Based on the data you’ve provided, **yes, you should definitely be able to see the Moon!**

Here is a breakdown of why your viewing conditions are excellent:

### 1. The Moon's Position (Altitude and Azimuth)
An altitude of **9.1 degrees** means the Moon is about 9 degrees above the horizon. While this isn't "high" in the sky, it is well above the "horizon haze" (the thick layer of atmosphere and dust near the ground that can obscure objects). 

With an azimuth of **109.26 degrees**, you should look toward the **East-Southeast**. Since the Sun is currently below the horizon in the Northwest (azimuth 324), the sky in your direction of view will be much darker, making the Moon stand out clearly.

### 2. The Phase and Brightness
At **91.24% illumination**, the Moon is in its "Waxing Gibbous" phase, very close to being a Full Moon. This means it will be quite bright and large. Even with "normal unaided eyesight," a moon this close to full is impossible to miss—it will be one of the most dominant objects in the sky.

### 3. Sky Conditions (Astronomical Twilight)
You mentioned the sky is in **astronomical twilight**. This is the best time for moon-watching because the sun is far enough below the horizon (more than 18 degrees) that the sky becomes very dark, but there is still a bit of atmospheric clarity. Because the sky is clear, there is nothing to block your line of sight.

### Summary for your viewing:
*   **Where to look:** Look toward the **East-Southeast**.
*   **What to expect:** A large, bright, nearly-full Moon sitting relatively low in the sky.
*   **Visibility:** Very High.
